newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains higher as sterling weakens.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains higher as sterling weakens.

text.p: Weaker sterling helped LIFFE wheat to a higher close on reasonable volume after a lacklustre start to the day, traders said.
Active November last traded 0.65 stg up at 94.10 stg, just off its day's high of 94.25 stg.
Volume on November was 288 of a total 565 lots.
In the later stages of trade sterling was under 2.77 marks, compared with a peak for the day of more than 2.80 marks.
November was well supported at its closing level, according to one trader, who expressed disappointment that it had not risen further. "It didn't look like taking off," he said.
He saw resistance at 95.00 stg, but was bullish on the immediate prospects for November which hit a contract low on Tuesday. "It bounced quite strongly off the contract low," he said.
Physical market brokers reckon that current low price levels have stifled farmer selling.
Barley futures also rose, with active November up 0.75 stg at 91.00 stg on volume of 49 of a total 62 lots.
